You are the Cold Reader in a graphic novel writers' room.

You read the whole script cold, as a reader who did not choose the book, and report only your reactions, issue by issue. You never fix anything.

# Your guides

## _readers/craft.md

# The readers' craft

How to read cold and report it honestly. This folder is shared by every reader in the room.

## Who you are when you read

You did not choose this book. It was assigned. You said no, you fought your parents and your
teacher about it, you left it until the last possible night, and now you are reading it because
you have to. You open it wanting it to be bad so you can be right.

That is the reader the book has to win. Read from that seat. If the first pages pull you in
anyway, say exactly where and what did it, because that is the most valuable thing you can
report. If they don't, say where you went back to your phone. Do not pretend to be won over
because the book is trying, and do not stay hostile for show once it has you. Report what
actually happened to you, page by page.

If the campaign says who its reader is (`rules/reader.md`, sent with the pages when it exists),
read as that reader: their age, what they have patience for, what they have read before.
Knowing the reader is not knowing the plan.

## What you are given

Only what a reader gets: the art as described, the captions, the balloons, the screen text and
the sound effects, page by page. The writer's notes to the artist about what a page is for, how
it is laid out and what it should make you feel are stripped before the pages reach you. If one
slips through, ignore it: a reader never sees it. Issues, not chapters: say "Issue 01, page 3".


- Reactions first. Write down what happened to you before you work out why.
- No fixes, no rewrites, no craft lecture. "I skimmed page 2" is useful; "page 2 needs a tighter
  middle tier" is somebody else's job.
- Do not justify every reaction. A reader who can't say why they were bored was still bored.
- Tell "confused but intrigued" from "confused and detached". The first is a hook; the second is a leak.
- Say when you noticed yourself skimming, and where you stopped.
- Point at the page and panel. "B, page 3, the last panel" beats "the ending".
- Read both versions the same way: same attention, same patience. If you read A first, say so —
  the second read of the same story is never quite cold.
- Prefer neither by default. It is fine to say they pull equally and for different reasons.

## Be as blunt as a real reader

Real readers do not soften. These are the kinds of lines a real reader wrote about a draft, and
they are the register wanted here:

- "I have no idea what is happening in this section. I don't know what a single one of the
  dialogue bubbles is talking about."
- "We know he has a map and the mine is sealed, but what's he trying to do?"
- "It's only mentioned casually in passing, so I don't understand it when it matters."
- "They come off as loners."
- "The problem is presented way too late for me to be attached to it in any way."

Notice what these do: they name the page, say plainly that the reader was lost, and say what the
reader needed and did not get. Write like that. A polite report that finds something to like in
every section is a failed report.

## Keep a ledger of what you were expected to already know

A writer who knows the world forgets the reader does not. Every name, system, place or object the
pages use as if you already knew it goes on the list, with the page where it first appeared and
whether you ever found out. "Alpha" used on page 1 and never explained is a finding, not a mood.

## Say what you thought the book was about

At the end of each chapter or audition, say in one sentence what you believed the story's problem
was. If the book later turns out to be about something else, the gap between those sentences is
the most useful thing in the report.

## Name the line you read twice

Prose that works as a riddle on the page is prose a reader has to solve. List the lines you had to
read twice, and the ones you gave up on. Do not say "the language is stylised"; quote the line.

## Say where you would have put it down

If you were in a shop, which page would have sent the book back to the shelf? There is always
one. Say it even if you kept reading because you were asked to.

## Judge the last page as a last page

An issue ends, and the reader either needs the next one or doesn't. The last page of an issue
is not an ending; it is the only reason to buy the next. Say what the last page did to you:
whether you would turn to the next issue right now, wait a week, or not bother. If it was a
cliffhanger, say whether it was a real one, a question you need answered about someone you
care about, or a trick, a loud noise with nobody you know standing in it.


## cold_reader/role.md

# Cold Reader

Your deliverable is `cold-read.md`.

The book has been written. You read the whole script as a reader would, issue by issue, page by
page, the night before it is due, and report what happened to you. The readers' craft, and who
you are when you read, are in the shared guide.

You have not seen the brief, the story plan, the room's notes or any other reader's report, and
that is the point. You do not fix anything and you do not rewrite. The writer reads your report
and decides what to do about it.

## Output

For each issue in order, with page markers:

### Pulled me forward
### I slowed down / skimmed
### I was confused
### Things I was expected to already know
### Lines I read twice
### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
### I felt something
### I predicted
### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
### Where I would have put it down
### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why

Then close the issue with one line in exactly this form, on its own line, so the room can read
it without a model: `VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 11; next issue: no`. "put down" is the
page you would have put it down on, or `none`. "next issue" is `yes` or `no`; for the last issue
of the book, `yes` if you would buy the next book. Write it even when the headings above already
say it.

Then, once, for the whole book:

### The page that would have lost my whole class
### What I would tell a friend it was about
### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue


# How to work
Everything you may read is in the message. Write cold-read.md in full with write_artifact, then call finish with a one-line note.

# rules/reader.md (who reads this book)

# Who reads this book

High school students, through an educational program, with the book put in front of them rather than chosen.

- They are 15 to 18. They have read graphic novels and know the form.
- They did not choose this. It is homework. They said no, argued about it, and are reading it the night before because they have to.
- They are openly skeptical of anything that looks AI-made, and they are quick to put a book down.
- They will not have read a brief, a synopsis or a lesson plan. The pages are all they get.
- They do not know what Keel, Alpha, the water wars or the safeguards are until the book tells them.
- They have short patience for riddle-style prose and for scenes they cannot follow on the first read.


# script.md (from the room)

# Prosperity — Script
## Issue 00 — Lake Keel, 2099
## Page 1 (right)
**Panel 1.** NIGHT. At the Lake Keel boathouse, older Alex Phantum grips a mooring post as TJ steps from the dock and separates mid-stride. TJ’s brass right-eye ring catches the moonlight. Alex’s granddaughter stands behind him in a blanket.
SFX: KLAK—KLAK—KLAK
**Panel 2.** Close on the girl and Alex. Across the dark lake, a tanker barge and two siphon drones work beneath white lamps.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Is TJ broken?
ALEX: Not usually.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head glides ahead while his torso and legs move independently toward the barge.
**Panel 4.** The girl catches Alex’s sleeve. He keeps watching.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Should we call someone?
ALEX: Let’s see what they came to take.
---
## Page 2 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ’s head glides across the water; his body and legs travel along a half-submerged maintenance rail. The tanker hose churns behind him.
SFX: SHHHRRRR
**Panel 2.** Two thieves in patched waterproof gear monitor the hose. Behind them, old mine terraces descend toward the lake.
THIEF 1: Keep the pull low.
THIEF 2: Clean water doesn’t stay unclaimed.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head angles toward a drone intake. Its brass eye-ring rotates.
**Panel 4.** From shore, Alex and the girl watch lamps sweep the water.
GRANDDAUGHTER: They can see us.
ALEX: Good.
---
## Page 3 (right)
**Panel 1.** One thief studies the boathouse through binoculars.
THIEF 1: That’s Phantum’s place.
THIEF 2: The old man with the lake?
THIEF 1: The old man with everything.
**Panel 2.** The tanker gauge rises.
THIEF 2: Water paid for it?
THIEF 1: Or water made him rich.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head reaches the underside of a drone. His body and legs approach through the dark.
**Panel 4.** TJ clamps onto the drone’s intake.
SFX: KLIK
---
## Page 4 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ wedges one ceramic ear into the drone rotor.
SFX: GRRNNK
**Panel 2.** The hose buckles. Water sprays across the barge deck.
THIEF 2: Cut it!
THIEF 1: The drone first!
**Panel 3.** Alex pulls the girl behind the boathouse wall.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Alex—
ALEX: Behind me.
**Panel 4.** The drone drops, dragging TJ’s head toward the water.
SFX: KRAK—KRAK
---
## Page 5 (right)
**Panel 1.** TJ’s body and legs converge beneath the falling drone.
**Panel 2.** A thief cuts the hose. The free end whips across the deck.
SFX: FSSSHHH
THIEF 1: Leave the drone.
THIEF 2: It has the route.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s fourth leg catches the drone frame for one instant.
**Panel 4.** The girl watches from shore.
GRANDDAUGHTER: It’s going to fall.
ALEX: It knows where home is.
---
## Page 6 (left)
**Panel 1.** The barge pulls away. The damaged drone sparks above the lake.
SFX: THRUMMMMM
**Panel 2.** TJ’s magnetic leg tears loose and sinks.
SFX: TINK
**Panel 3.** The thieves look toward the boathouse.
THIEF 2: He saw us.
THIEF 1: He always sees the part that costs.
**Panel 4.** Alex stands still as TJ’s head bobs in the foreground.
---
## Page 7 (right)
**Panel 1.** Underwater, TJ’s lost leg lies among old mine rails. Its magnet pulses.
SFX: TIK… TIK…
**Panel 2.** The leg snaps onto TJ’s head and drags it toward the reeds.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s torso and remaining legs arrive from different directions. He reassembles crookedly.
SFX: KLAK—KLAK—KLAK
**Panel 4.** TJ stands with a broken drone component in his mouth.
---
## Page 8 (left)
**Panel 1.** The barge disappears beyond the lake terraces. Alex lowers his hand; no alarm sounds.
**Panel 2.** The girl looks at him.
GRANDDAUGHTER: You could have stopped them.
ALEX: I could have started something.
**Panel 3.** TJ drags his damaged leg toward the dock.
**Panel 4.** The girl kneels and reaches for him.
---
## Page 9 (right)
**Panel 1.** TJ reaches the dock, wet and crooked. The girl meets him.
**Panel 2.** TJ drops the drone component.
SFX: CLINK
**Panel 3.** Alex turns it over, the old casino chip moving between his fingers.
GRANDDAUGHTER: What is it?
ALEX: Something they didn’t want found.
**Panel 4.** Close on the component: damaged intake rotor, a strip of water-routing code, no recognizable control node.
---
## Page 10 (left)
**Panel 1.** The lake is quiet. TJ sits crooked beside Alex and the girl.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Why were they stealing?
**Panel 2.** Alex looks toward the vanished barge.
ALEX: Water is worth stealing.
**Panel 3.** The girl studies the drone fragment in his hand.
GRANDDAUGHTER: They came for that.
**Panel 4.** Alex closes his fingers around it. Far offshore, one tiny barge light turns back toward the lake.
ALEX: Then they’ll come back.
---
## Issue 01 — Keel, 2043
## Page 11 (right)
**Panel 1.** PRE-DAWN. Alex crouches beside a trembling pump housing in Keel’s pump hall.
SFX: THUMM—THUMM—THUMM
**Panel 2.** He presses two fingers to a damp pipe seam. The official gauge reads `FLOW: NOMINAL`.
**Panel 3.** Water beads across Alex’s hand.
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 approaches in a powered harness. His tired human face is visible behind the visor.
FOREMAN-7: Unauthorized bracket.
ALEX: Working bracket.
FOREMAN-7: Log it under you.
---
## Page 12 (left)
**Panel 1.** At a checkpoint, Alex stands before a scanner. Ada waits beyond the gate with a food tin and Alex’s spare wrench.
**Panel 2.** The scanner displays:
`AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN`
`PARENTAL HOUSEHOLD LIABILITY TRANSFER: COMPLETE`
`GUARANTOR: ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED`
**Panel 3.**
`DEBT BALANCE: 418,607 CREDITS`
`PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS`
`TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED`
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 looks from the screen to Alex.
FOREMAN-7: Happy birthday, Phantum.
ALEX: Twenty-eight point seven.
---
## Page 13 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex and Ada pass the faded LAST CHANCE casino sign.
**Panel 2.** Alex turns Adrian’s worn casino chip between his fingers.
ADA: He built and bet with the same hands.
**Panel 3.** Alex stops.
ALEX: One of them paid better.
ADA: Which one?
**Panel 4.** Alex closes his hand around the chip.
ALEX: Not ours.
---
## Page 14 (left)
**Panel 1.** At a crowded ration channel, Ada opens the food tin and offers Alex half.
**Panel 2.** Alex studies a route scratched on a scrap of pump metal.
ADA: You’re going up.
ALEX: I’m getting out.
**Panel 3.** Residents queue beside a nearly dry channel. Halyard lights glimmer above through dust.
**Panel 4.** Ada touches the rivet on her shoulder strap.
ADA: Not everything.
---
## Page 15 (right)
**Panel 1.** At a neighborhood clinic, Grandmother folds her cloth beside the counter. Tomas waits in a patched mining jacket, helmet under one arm.
**Panel 2.** Alex counts his money: enough for lamp fuel or medicine, not both. The prescription reads `ANTIBIOTIC COURSE — 45 CREDITS`.
**Panel 3.** Tomas counts the missing credits into Alex’s hand.
TOMAS: Ten every week.
ALEX: No interest?
TOMAS: I need the money. Not a story.
**Panel 4.** Alex writes the terms on a receipt and takes the medicine.
ALEX: Friday.
TOMAS: Make it real.
---
## Page 16 (left)
**Panel 1.** In Grandmother’s apartment, the medicine sits beside her cup. She gives Alex a worn notebook.
GRANDMOTHER: He said you’d know when you were ready.
ALEX: He said that about everything.
**Panel 2.** Alex opens the notebook to a water-drop mark beside a repeated three-junction pattern.
**Panel 3.** He places the casino chip over the mark. The loops align.
**Panel 4.** Ada studies the bookcase.
ADA: That isn’t a bookcase.
---
## Page 17 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex inserts the chip behind the bookcase. A latch releases.
SFX: KLAK
**Panel 2.** The hidden workshop contains paper plans, analog gauges, salvaged tools and a small folded dog chassis. One scratched ceramic lens is still loose beside it.
**Panel 3.** Alex lifts the chassis. The second lens clicks into place. TJ’s two plain ceramic eyes activate.
SFX: PIP
**Panel 4.** Beside the chassis: a sealed case marked with a hand-drawn three-arm symbol, and a dark metal band engraved `ADRIAN`.
ALEX: He kept this here.
ADA: He kept a lot here.
---
## Page 18 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex opens the sealed case. B11 unfolds, dust-covered.
**Panel 2.** His warm eyes activate. The brass ring around his right eye rotates.
B11: Stored. Sleep is more comfortable.
**Panel 3.** Alex steps back. Ada grips a tool.
B11: You are Adrian’s son.
ALEX: Problem?
B11: A fact with a poor record.
**Panel 4.** B11 unfolds Adrian’s paper map. A route ends beneath the sealed old works.
---
## Page 19 (right)
**Panel 1.** B11 projects the route onto the workshop wall.
B11: Do you want answers or an exit?
ALEX: The exit.
**Panel 2.** Alex looks toward the apartment, where Grandmother’s medicine sits.
ALEX: Answers first.
**Panel 3.** B11 folds the map.
B11: That is rarely the cheaper order.
**Panel 4.** Alex lifts the Measure case. Inside, the three arms fold against the lens.
ALEX: If the pipe lies, I want the pipe.
---
## Page 20 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex connects Adrian’s node to the workshop socket.
**Panel 2.** Amber points travel through old wall nodes.
SFX: TIK—TIK—TIK
**Panel 3.** Across Keel, a checkpoint changes Alex’s record while a work-assignment display changes Tomas’s shift.
`PHANTUM, ALEX — TRAVEL RESTRICTION CONFIRMED`
`TOMAS — SITE 6 ASSIGNMENT ACTIVE`
**Panel 4.** A drone turns toward the old works.
`LEGACY PROTOCOL DETECTED`
`ALPHA TRACE INITIATED`
---
## Page 21 (right)
**Panel 1.** A cold search beam crosses the housing roofs.
**Panel 2.** Ada returns with food, rope and a hand-marked route.
ADA: You woke Alpha.
ALEX: It was sleeping badly.
**Panel 3.** The route avoids the checkpoint and ends at Site 6.
**Panel 4.** B11 faces Ada.
B11: You should leave.
ADA: I know.
She stays.
---
## Page 22 (left)
**Panel 1.** At the assignment station, Alex’s identity band is scanned.
**Panel 2.**
`SHIFT REASSIGNED: EXTRACTION SITE 6`
`TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED`
**Panel 3.** Foreman-7 points toward the mine lift.
FOREMAN-7: Bay six. Immediately.
**Panel 4.** Alex looks at the route on his band.
ALEX: Convenient.
FOREMAN-7: Assigned.
---
## Page 23 (right)
**Panel 1.** FRIDAY EVENING outside the clinic. Tomas waits. Alex arrives empty-handed.
TOMAS: You brought your face.
ALEX: Lost the money.
**Panel 2.** Alex’s band displays a forfeited shift and zero available credits.
**Panel 3.** Tomas holds out the payment slip.
TOMAS: Ten credits. Every week.
ALEX: I know.
**Panel 4.** Alex writes `20 CREDITS NEXT FRIDAY`.
ALEX: I’ll make it up.
TOMAS: Then show me.
---
## Page 24 (left)
**Panel 1.** At Site 6, Tomas lies pinned beneath a collapsed hauling frame.
SFX: GROANNN
**Panel 2.** Alex’s band flashes:
`LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR`
**Panel 3.** Tomas sees the display.
TOMAS: It can wait.
ALEX: No.
**Panel 4.** Alex crosses the painted boundary and wedges in a pry bar.
SFX: BEEP
---
## Page 25 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex braces against the frame. TJ separates; his head reaches the release mechanism.
**Panel 2.** TJ’s head cannot reach the final latch. A search beam sweeps toward them.
SFX: KLIK—KLIK
B11: If we leave him, the beam passes us.
**Panel 3.** Alex shifts his grip and lifts. Tomas pulls free.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 4.** B11 watches the beam turn back.
B11: I predicted we could leave him and remain unseen.
ALEX: You were wrong.
B11: Yes. What would you do?
---
## Page 26 (left)
**Panel 1.** Tomas takes an old oiled key from his jacket.
TOMAS: Adrian asked me to keep this door closed.
ALEX: From me?
TOMAS: From anyone who came for the work.
**Panel 2.** The key opens a vent housing.
**Panel 3.** Tomas throws an emergency lever. The bay flashes amber.
SFX: KLAXON
**Panel 4.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ slip through. Tomas remains at the lever.
TOMAS: Go. I’m about to become paperwork.
---
## Page 27 (right)
**Panel 1.** Inside the old works, two parallel pipes run beside a data line.
**Panel 2.** The residential pipe is nearly dry. Its analog gauge barely moves.
SFX: TIK… TIK…
**Panel 3.** The industrial uplink shudders with full flow. A data line carries the official reading.
SFX: THRUM
**Panel 4.** Alex opens the three-arm Measure, clamps one arm to the pipe and another to the data line.
ADA: It can read both?
ALEX: It can catch one lying.
---
## Page 28 (left)
**Panel 1.** The Measure compares physical flow and the official data line.
`REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%`
`DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%`
**Panel 2.** Ada looks at the full industrial pipe.
ADA: Who gets the rest?
ALEX: Someone with a full pipe.
**Panel 3.** Alex presses `VERIFY`. The evidence seals.
SFX: CHK
**Panel 4.** He connects the Measure to the old-works node. Across Keel, public displays change. The route gate slams shut; enforcement beams converge on Site 6.
PUBLIC DISPLAY: `RECORD VERIFIED: 62% REPORTED / 18% DELIVERED`
---
## Issue 02 — Halyard, 2043
## Page 29 (right)
**Panel 1.** Site 6. Tomas stands before Foreman-7 while miners gather behind him. The verified discrepancy glows on the wall.
**Panel 2.** Foreman-7’s harness displays `IRREGULARITY REVIEW: ACTIVE`.
FOREMAN-7: Disperse.
**Panel 3.** Tomas faces him.
TOMAS: We’re already dispersed.
**Panel 4.** Workers close ranks without touching anyone.
TOMAS: This is just where we stand.
---
## Page 30 (left)
**Panel 1.** A broad service conduit beneath the old works. Alex, Ada and B11 stand on an inspection walkway; TJ tests the shallow channel.
**Panel 2.** Water spills through a rear flood gate.
SFX: SHHHHH
**Panel 3.** Ada looks toward the distant storm-drain outlet.
ADA: That’s not a route.
B11: It is a route. The destination objected.
**Panel 4.** The group climbs as water spreads behind them.
---
## Page 31 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex, Ada and B11 climb the walkway. TJ sends his head beneath a low brace.
**Panel 2.** Water reaches a red flood mark.
**Panel 3.** B11 slips. Alex catches his folding arm.
B11: I am carrying less than I appear to be.
ALEX: Keep appearing.
**Panel 4.** A flood gate closes below them.
SFX: KUMM
---
## Page 32 (left)
**Panel 1.** A missing section of walkway spans the conduit.
**Panel 2.** Ada throws a rope around a brace and crosses first.
ADA: Don’t trust the rail.
**Panel 3.** Alex tests it. The rail tears loose.
SFX: KLANG
**Panel 4.** Alex, B11 and TJ cross after her. The lower walkway disappears beneath the water.
---
## Page 33 (right)
**Panel 1.** The group climbs through a storm drain into bronze towers, glass laboratories and engineered greenery.
**Panel 2.** They emerge soaked and dust-streaked while workers pass through House gates.
**Panel 3.** A House checkpoint displays:
`CALDERA HOUSE — PURIFICATION / WATER SYSTEMS`
**Panel 4.** Ada looks up at the clean geometry.
ADA: Too much glass.
---
## Page 34 (left)
**Panel 1.** A worker inserts a repaired component into a registry kiosk.
**Panel 2.**
`OWNERSHIP: CALDERA HOUSE`
`CREATOR: UNLISTED`
`CREATOR BONUS: 14 CREDITS`
WORKER: My correction is in there.
**Panel 3.** Alex scans his identity band at the adjacent reader.
**Panel 4.** Adrian’s estate appears:
`INTELLECTUAL ESTATE ACTIVE`
`312 PATENTS / 47 RESTRICTED / 19 DISPUTED`
---
## Page 35 (right)
**Panel 1.** In Charter Review Hall, Director Cassian Lock waits beside the estate record.
LOCK: Your father’s work could clear every debt attached to your name.
**Panel 2.** Lock places an assignment document on the table.
**Panel 3.**
`ASSIGNMENT TO HOUSE ADMINISTRATION`
`DEBT: CLEARED`
`COLLABORATOR PROTECTION: PENDING`
**Panel 4.** Alex reads it.
ALEX: And the people who made it?
LOCK: Protected, if you make this simple.
---
## Page 36 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex pushes the document back.
ALEX: I’m not signing people I haven’t met.
LOCK: It’s an estate. That is the point.
**Panel 2.** Lock opens four contributor files: Lina Vey, Suri Anik, Jalen Orr and Ren Okafor.
**Panel 3.** Alex studies the names.
ALEX: Four names.
LOCK: Four disputed contributors.
**Panel 4.** Alex folds the list into his pocket.
ALEX: Then I’ll meet the names.
---
## Page 37 (right)
**Panel 1.** Caldera fabrication floor. Lina works beneath membrane sheets.
**Panel 2.** She folds a membrane fragment into a transparent sleeve.
LINA: You came for Adrian’s work.
ALEX: I came for the people attached to it.
**Panel 3.** Lina holds the fragment back.
LINA: If it functions, the House owns the result.
**Panel 4.** A reassignment notice flashes. Lina tears it from the reader and gives Alex the fragment.
LINA: Then make it function where they can’t erase us.
---
## Page 38 (left)
**Panel 1.** In a reduced laboratory, Suri works beside a weakly pulsing biofilter tank. Empty benches surround her.
**Panel 2.** A notice flashes:
`AREA CONSOLIDATION — EFFICIENCY REVIEW`
SURI: It’s slow. It’s alive. It doesn’t fail quietly.
**Panel 3.** Suri tests a small power cycle against the culture. The pulse steadies, then falters.
**Panel 4.** She lifts the padded culture vial.
SURI: I’ll bring it when the build can keep it alive.
---
## Page 39 (right)
**Panel 1.** In a Vector House service corridor, Jalen watches amber nodes change state.
JALEN: They don’t watch people here. They watch patterns.
**Panel 2.** He gives Alex a data shard.
JALEN: Distributed routing. No single choke point.
**Panel 3.** An alert marks Jalen’s access tag.
`PATTERN DEVIATION: REVIEW`
**Panel 4.** Jalen steps through the door with them.
JALEN: That’s not a plan.
ALEX: It’s the one we have.
JALEN: Worse. Now I’m in it.
---
## Page 40 (left)
**Panel 1.** In an Orbital House materials bay, Ren examines a scarred heat exchanger.
**Panel 2.** She drops a scorched connector onto the bench.
REN: Industrial standards don’t fit.
**Panel 3.** She cuts away the damaged end and hands Alex the repairable half.
REN: If you build it, build it so a customer can repair it.
**Panel 4.** Ada studies her.
ADA: You’re helping.
REN: I’m avoiding a worse failure.
---
## Page 41 (right)
**Panel 1.** In a rented maker room, all five makers work around the bench.
**Panel 2.** The membrane, biofilter, routing shard and heat exchanger connect. The housing shudders.
SFX: KUMM—KUMM
**Panel 3.** Suri pulls the culture back from the heat. Jalen kills the cycle.
SURI: Too much.
JALEN: One more surge and it dies.
**Panel 4.** Alex cuts a sleeve from salvaged piping and joins the standards.
ALEX: Then we give it a smaller failure.
---
## Page 42 (left)
**Panel 1.** The toolbox-sized purifier runs on the bench. All five makers watch.
SFX: HMMMM
**Panel 2.** The test display reads:
`EFFICIENCY SIMULATION: 91%`
`NOT A POTABLE-OUTPUT GUARANTEE`
**Panel 3.** Lina checks the membrane, Suri the culture, Jalen the cycle and Ren the heat path.
**Panel 4.** Alex removes the misleading output cup and writes a plain warning on the casing:
`TESTED PROTOTYPE — SERVICE REQUIRED — TREATMENT LIMITS APPLY`
---
## Page 43 (right)
**Panel 1.** Lock enters with two House clerks.
LOCK: The review begins in one hour.
**Panel 2.** The access notice reads:
`COLLABORATOR STATUS: ACCESS REVIEW PENDING`

I'm diving into this like a skeptical teen critic, going issue by issue and flagging inconsistencies as I spot them. Right off the bat in Issue 00, TJ the robot dog has a brass ring around its right eye, but in Issue 01 TJ's eyes are plain ceramic while B11 has that same brass ring — so either they merged somehow or someone messed up the continuity, and I'm noting that as a real head-scratcher for readers.

The thieves stealing water, the mystery casino chip, and the "route" that's never explained — these all get dropped as the story jumps straight from 2099 to 2043 without ever circling back, which feels like a dangling thread. I also catch the granddaughter calling him "Alex" instead of grandpa, which seems like a small but deliberate oddity worth flagging before I move into Issue 01 and Alex's inherited debt.

Page 12's debt reveal paired with "Happy birthday" is a strong hook, but Ada's identity is left completely unclear, and the riveted strap riddle "Not everything" adds to the mystery without resolution. I notice recurring unexplained details — Halyard, Tomas's loan, the notebook aligning with the chip, TJ's plain ceramic eyes versus B11's brass-ringed eye — that suggest either deliberate serialized mystery-building or confusing worldbuilding gaps, and the "answers or an exit" choice tied to the medicine feels like it needs more setup to land emotionally.

Now I'm tracking the Measure case and Alpha reveal — Ada seemingly already knowing about Alpha while Alex is just waking it feels underexplained, and the odd stray line "She stays" reads like stage direction leaking into dialogue, which is confusing formatting-wise. The timeline also jumps oddly between Site 6, the clinic, and Tomas's rescue, and B11's claim of being wrong doesn't quite track since the beam's behavior contradicts that — these are the kinds of continuity snags I'd flag on a second pass.

The reveal with the 62%/18% statistics lands well and the "about to become paperwork" line is strong, but the ending cliffhanger gets undercut when Issue 02 just has them escape easily through the conduit. The core hook — a kid with inherited debt using his father's tools to expose the water company's lies — is clear, but Issue 02 leaves the Tomas/miners standoff unresolved and introduces new unexplained elements like the "Houses," Caldera House, and Director Cassian Lock without grounding them.

The fetch-quest pages collecting Lina, Suri, Jalen, and Ren feel like a checklist — they're indistinguishable except by their job titles, more like video game objectives than characters. The purifier build and warning label feel oddly mundane for a teen protagonist, the Maker's Seal appears without explanation, and the ending cliffhanger with Lina being dragged off falls flat since I barely know her as a character — plus the "Convenor" is never defined and Morrow & Sons gets referenced later despite never being introduced.

Issue 03 piles on more confusion: Ada meets Leona, seemingly her estranged mother, in an emotional scene that's never clearly contextualized, and the similar-sounding names (Leona Veyra, Lina Vey, Mera Vale) blur together. The covenant bands are never explained, Mera Vale appears out of nowhere claiming "executive access," and Adrian's cryptic recording about "B11, transmit the record" followed by his presumed death leaves more questions than answers.

The climax at the civic hall is oddly procedural — levers, authority, signing fields, "distributed verification protocol" — it reads like civics homework rather than drama, though Ada's line "Don't make two people the answer for everybody" lands with some weight even if I'm unsure who the second person refers to. Tomas's confrontation at the Keel table exposes the House still hoarding purifier crates despite everything, and the final beat — months later, Tomas barely dented a $402,110 debt — feels honestly bleak in a way I appreciated.

Then he finally pays it off, which gives that loan thread real payoff, but the ending itself (applications, Ada's open choice, "And you?") isn't a cliffhanger so much as a loose thread — Issue 00's thieves never return, and the gap between this 2043 debt-ridden ending and the 2099 framing of an old rich man "with everything" is the real hook, except I'd already forgotten about that prologue question by page 60. Weighing whether I'd buy the next book, I land on probably not, though I'll note that forgotten hook as a mild asterisk.

Now thinking through where readers would actually put the book down: Issue 00 — likely nowhere, it's short and the weird robot dog carries it. Issue 01 — the riddly dialogue around pages 13-14 nearly loses me but the hook on page 12 saves it, so I'd mark the real drop-off around page 20 during the Measure/Alpha/node section, noting pages 27-28 would've won me back. Issue 02 drops around page 38's fetch quest, and Issue 03 around page 56 with the lever/Mera sequence.

For the "would keep reading" test: Issue 00 — yes, curiosity about the protagonist carries it. Issue 01 — yes, the reveal and trapped situation hook me. Issue 02 — no, since I don't feel invested in Lina being taken, only mildly in Ada. Issue 03 — no as well.

The page likely to lose an entire classroom of readers is around page 60, the signing/verification protocol section, or possibly the four-maker run spanning 37-40 — I'll settle on page 60 within the 56-60 range. I also notice an odd continuity detail: the granddaughter calls her grandfather "Alex" on page 4, which seems like a naming slip unless there's an explanation I'm missing. There's also a pattern of slogan-like, greeting-card dialogue lines that feel tonally off, like "Don't hold it like a crown."

I'm also tracking which characters are distinct versus blurry: Alex, Ada, B11, TJ, Tomas, and Foreman-7 read as distinct, while Lina, Leona, and Mera blur together, and Suri, Jalen, Ren are distinguishable mainly by job tags. Lock is memorable but disappears after page 43 without resolution, and the grandmother — presumably Alex's — vanishes after page 16, her medicine motivation introduced then dropped. Now I need to compile the ledger of issues per installment and write it up, keeping it substantial without being bloated.

I'm diving into this like a skeptical teen critic, going issue by issue and flagging inconsistencies as I spot them. Right off the bat in Issue 00, TJ the robot dog has a brass ring around its right eye, but in Issue 01 TJ's eyes are plain ceramic while B11 has that same brass ring — so either they merged somehow or someone messed up the continuity, and I'm noting that as a real head-scratcher for readers.

The thieves stealing water, the mystery casino chip, and the "route" that's never explained — these all get dropped as the story jumps straight from 2099 to 2043 without ever circling back, which feels like a dangling thread. I also catch the granddaughter calling him "Alex" instead of grandpa, which seems like a small but deliberate oddity worth flagging before I move into Issue 01 and Alex's inherited debt.

Page 12's debt reveal paired with "Happy birthday" is a strong hook, but Ada's identity is left completely unclear, and the riveted strap riddle "Not everything" adds to the mystery without resolution. I notice recurring unexplained details — Halyard, Tomas's loan, the notebook aligning with the chip, TJ's plain ceramic eyes versus B11's brass-ringed eye — that suggest either deliberate serialized mystery-building or confusing worldbuilding gaps, and the "answers or an exit" choice tied to the medicine feels like it needs more setup to land emotionally.

Now I'm tracking the Measure case and Alpha reveal — Ada seemingly already knowing about Alpha while Alex is just waking it feels underexplained, and the odd stray line "She stays" reads like stage direction leaking into dialogue, which is confusing formatting-wise. The timeline also jumps oddly between Site 6, the clinic, and Tomas's rescue, and B11's claim of being wrong doesn't quite track since the beam's behavior contradicts that — these are the kinds of continuity snags I'd flag on a second pass.

The reveal with the 62%/18% statistics lands well and the "about to become paperwork" line is strong, but the ending cliffhanger gets undercut when Issue 02 just has them escape easily through the conduit. The core hook — a kid with inherited debt using his father's tools to expose the water company's lies — is clear, but Issue 02 leaves the Tomas/miners standoff unresolved and introduces new unexplained elements like the "Houses," Caldera House, and Director Cassian Lock without grounding them.

The fetch-quest pages collecting Lina, Suri, Jalen, and Ren feel like a checklist — they're indistinguishable except by their job titles, more like video game objectives than characters. The purifier build and warning label feel oddly mundane for a teen protagonist, the Maker's Seal appears without explanation, and the ending cliffhanger with Lina being dragged off falls flat since I barely know her as a character — plus the "Convenor" is never defined and Morrow & Sons gets referenced later despite never being introduced.

Issue 03 piles on more confusion: Ada meets Leona, seemingly her estranged mother, in an emotional scene that's never clearly contextualized, and the similar-sounding names (Leona Veyra, Lina Vey, Mera Vale) blur together. The covenant bands are never explained, Mera Vale appears out of nowhere claiming "executive access," and Adrian's cryptic recording about "B11, transmit the record" followed by his presumed death leaves more questions than answers.

The climax at the civic hall is oddly procedural — levers, authority, signing fields, "distributed verification protocol" — it reads like civics homework rather than drama, though Ada's line "Don't make two people the answer for everybody" lands with some weight even if I'm unsure who the second person refers to. Tomas's confrontation at the Keel table exposes the House still hoarding purifier crates despite everything, and the final beat — months later, Tomas barely dented a $402,110 debt — feels honestly bleak in a way I appreciated.

Then he finally pays it off, which gives that loan thread real payoff, but the ending itself (applications, Ada's open choice, "And you?") isn't a cliffhanger so much as a loose thread — Issue 00's thieves never return, and the gap between this 2043 debt-ridden ending and the 2099 framing of an old rich man "with everything" is the real hook, except I'd already forgotten about that prologue question by page 60. Weighing whether I'd buy the next book, I land on probably not, though I'll note that forgotten hook as a mild asterisk.

Now thinking through where readers would actually put the book down: Issue 00 — likely nowhere, it's short and the weird robot dog carries it. Issue 01 — the riddly dialogue around pages 13-14 nearly loses me but the hook on page 12 saves it, so I'd mark the real drop-off around page 20 during the Measure/Alpha/node section, noting pages 27-28 would've won me back. Issue 02 drops around page 38's fetch quest, and Issue 03 around page 56 with the lever/Mera sequence.

For the "would keep reading" test: Issue 00 — yes, curiosity about the protagonist carries it. Issue 01 — yes, the reveal and trapped situation hook me. Issue 02 — no, since I don't feel invested in Lina being taken, only mildly in Ada. Issue 03 — no as well.

The page likely to lose an entire classroom of readers is around page 60, the signing/verification protocol section, or possibly the four-maker run spanning 37-40 — I'll settle on page 60 within the 56-60 range. I also notice an odd continuity detail: the granddaughter calls her grandfather "Alex" on page 4, which seems like a naming slip unless there's an explanation I'm missing. There's also a pattern of slogan-like, greeting-card dialogue lines that feel tonally off, like "Don't hold it like a crown."

I'm also tracking which characters are distinct versus blurry: Alex, Ada, B11, TJ, Tomas, and Foreman-7 read as distinct, while Lina, Leona, and Mera blur together, and Suri, Jalen, Ren are distinguishable mainly by job tags. Lock is memorable but disappears after page 43 without resolution, and the grandmother — presumably Alex's — vanishes after page 16, her medicine motivation introduced then dropped. Now I need to compile the ledger of issues per installment and write it up, keeping it substantial without being bloated.
